mustFix.measured: The draft's qualifying set is 29 = 32 minus {DR-128, DR-129, DR-130}. The adopted qualifying set is 23 = D-002's 21 plus DR-131 and DR-133 (D-134), and the adopted deferral limb has nine members: DR-106, DR-108, DR-109, DR-110, DR-113, DR-116, DR-128, DR-129, DR-130. Under the adopted set the true report is: 6 of 23 SATISFIED-requiring rows SATISFIED (DR-102, DR-104, DR-115, DR-117, DR-119, DR-123 — all six lie inside D-002's 21); among the 23: 14 OPEN (DR-101, 103, 105, 111, 112, 114, 120, 121, 124, 125, 126, 127, 131, 133), 1 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED (DR-118), 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW (DR-107, DR-122); 6+14+1+2 = 23; the nine deferral-limb rows all carry lead label OPEN; 14+9 = 23 OPEN overall; 23+9 = 32. The draft's rule — a row is on the deferral limb only if its own file-08 cell says it does not reach slice 1 — appears in no adopted text. It is the draft's own criterion, and it silently drops six D-002 deferrals whose file-08 cells read bare 'OPEN' or 'OPEN / inherits hard blockers'. The draft also never mentions D-134, the one adopted entry that already places rows on 'the deferral limb' by that name and fixes the set's cardinality.
mustFix.whyItLands: The entry exists to make the snapshot report the qualifying set instead of the row total. The qualifying set is an adopted object with a recorded cardinality (23) and a recorded change procedure (a D-000-reviewed scoped D-002 successor, D-132 clause 3 / D-134). Writing '6 of 29 slice-affecting rows' and '3 of 32 on the deferral limb' into file 08 would record a third number that matches neither the row total the snapshot has carried (32, which D-134 knowingly kept: 'After the later MF-6 act the snapshot becomes 4 of 32') nor the adopted set (23). That is a change to D-002's affected-row set made under a header that says 'Does not amend ... D-002', without D-132-style authorization, and without naming the six rows it moves back onto the SATISFIED limb. The draft's own premise — 'rows are authoritative; if this block and a row disagree, the row wins' — cuts the other way for those six: their cells are silent about slice 1, and D-002 requires each deferral to get 'its recorded disposition, never silence'; the snapshot cannot cure that silence by counting them as slice-affecting. The draft's Alternatives bullet 4 rejects reading the limb over 'any OPEN row with any deferral language' but never considers the actual alternative: reading it over the rows D-002 and D-134 put there.
mustFix.remedy: Either (a) re-measure against the adopted set: 6 of 23 SATISFIED-requiring rows SATISFIED (D-002 set as amended by D-134); 9 of 32 on the deferral limb — DR-106, DR-109, DR-113 (D-002, deferred wholly), DR-108 (D-001 slice-conditional; D-002: no credential-requiring features), DR-110 (D-002: fresh signed download in slice 1), DR-116 (D-002: no third-party support policy yet), DR-128 (D-002 / file 10), DR-129 (D-002), DR-130 (D-010 / C-D010) — with the among-the-23 split 14 OPEN, 1 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, and note that six deferral-limb cells carry no in-cell disposition and stay governed by D-002 (their recording in-cell, if wanted, is a separate MF-6 entry per D-002's 'own artifact and commit'). Cite D-002 line 453, D-134, D-056 line 3381 and D-001 line 188 as the governing text, and put the condition-2 qualifying-set rule into the snapshot preamble beside condition 1's (see CLAUDE-D365-SF3). Or (b) if the coordinator wants the draft's cell-self-declaration rule, say so as a scoped D-002/D-134 successor that moves DR-106/108/109/110/113/116 from the deferral limb to the SATISFIED-requiring set, name the authority for that scope change, and remove 'Does not amend ... D-002' and 'does not decide product scope' — because under (b) the entry does decide it.
